beats.narration_text: Someone asked whether Claude decides on its own when it writes a cease and desist letter. It doesn't decide — it follows steps. So: when Claude writes one, is it just following steps?

shot.new_visual_element: Writer types 'When Claude writes a cease and desist, is it deciding?', hesitates on 'deciding', corrects to 'following steps', lands the real question

beats.note: B00 is Remotion (BrutalistHesitantWriter) per hai-simple SKILL.md WRITER LAW. TIMING LAW: 20-35 word narration + lead_silence_s 0.8 to give the typing a >=9s window; verify media/B00.mp4 >= 8s and that the correction ('deciding' -> 'following steps') lands on screen.

beats.narration_text: A Skill is a folder Claude reads before it acts. This one is called cease-desist. Its one file, SKILL.md, holds the whole instruction set, written in plain language — no hidden logic. Claude reads it, then acts. The file is the program.
The instructions live in a Steps section. Claude reads each step in order and executes it — read the file, execute each step, return the result. Linear: no branching, unless a step says otherwise.

production_viz.label: READ, EXECUTE, RETURN
production_viz.caption: linear — no branching unless a step says so

beats.narration_text: One instruction inside it is specific: the internal draft, the pre-send brief, and the triage memo are all marked as attorney work product — internal legal material. The letter that actually goes out isn't marked that way, because it's written to be read by the other side, not kept as an internal file.

production_viz.label: WHAT CARRIES THE HEADER
production_viz.caption: written for the other side, not filed internally

beats.narration_text: Claude isn't deciding what belongs in the letter — it's following the SKILL.md, one step at a time, and only doing what that file says.

props.quote: Claude isn't deciding what belongs in the letter — it's following the SKILL.md, one step at a time, and only doing what that file says.
props.sparkLine: Follows the file. Only the file.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude: I think someone is using my brand name without permission. Read the cease-desist skill, and before you draft anything, walk me through exactly what you'll do — what steps you'll follow, what you need from me, and what stays out of the letter.
